title: Progressive deployment: compatibility guards and geo-tiered fallback routing
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We need a safe, observable progressive deployment path for model variants that enforces compatibility checks, prefers regional locality, and degrades along defined capacity tiers when necessary. Current rollouts rely on simple traffic splits and single-region fallbacks which have led to cache incoherence, unpredictable latency spikes when a region is saturated, and occasional silent quality regressions for a small subset of customers.

Goal: Implement a routing and fallback orchestration layer used during canary, A/B, and shadow deployments that performs three responsibilities: (1) run deterministic compatibility checks at deploy-time (schema, KV cache layout, kv-cache version), (2) apply region-aware routing policies that prefer local-region, then sibling region, then cross-region with warmup routing, and (3) tiered capacity fallback: traffic should step down through a list of compatible model variants (same family, quantized variant, lower-seq-length variant) before failing over to a lower SLA tier or returning a graceful degraded response.

Scope: API + control plane policy extension, runtime routing logic, deployment-time compatibility verifier, rollout orchestration (canary -> ramp -> A/B -> full), observability (per-variant latency/cost/quality), and auto-rollback triggers for both quality and infra anomalies.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Deploy-time verifier rejects model variants that fail schema or kv-cache compatibility checks and surfaces clear error messages in the deployment UI/CLI.
2) Canary traffic can be routed with a geo preference policy: local-region first (>=90% preference), then sibling-region warmup, then cross-region fallback. Routes are configurable per-environment.
3) Tiered fallback list is enforced atomically for an incoming request: primary variant -> quantized compatible -> lower-seq-length variant -> dedicated capacity pool -> graceful degraded response. No duplicate routing or request duplication outside intentional shadowing.
4) Auto-rollback conditions configurable: quality delta (on eval set) > 6% degrade OR 95th percentile latency increase > 2x OR 5xx error rate > 1% over a 5-minute window. Rollback completes within configured timeout and triggers notifications.
5) End-to-end integration tests for canary, A/B, and shadow scenarios pass in CI with simulated region failures.
6) Dashboards expose variant-level P50/P95 latency, error rate, tokens/unit cost, and a canary health score. Alerts route to #infra-incident and owner on call.
7) No data-lose scenarios: KV cache migrations or format changes are blocked unless explicit migration plan provided.
implementation_notes:
High level tasks:
- Add deployment-time compatibility verifier (CLI + control plane). Checks: model input/output schema, tokenizer checksum, kv-cache layout version, attention config compatibility. Fail fast with mitigation suggestions.
- Extend control plane policy DSL to express: geo preference, sibling-region order, tiered-variant-list with weights, and warmup windows.
- Runtime routing: implement region-aware routing middleware with circuit-breaker per-variant and capacity-tier tracking. Use pins for 'dedicated pool' routes.
- Auto-rollback service: consume metrics from metrics pipeline, compute canary health score, and execute rollback API (with optional paused manual approve).
- Shadowing: allow n% of traffic as passive shadow to candidate variants (no KV writes) and capture outputs for quality eval.
- KV-cache migration guard: require explicit migration flag and optional shadow-migration mode to validate cache correctness.
- Backwards compatibility matrix: maintain in repo as CSV with columns: model_family, variant, tokenizer_hash, kv_version, compatible_with_list.

Implementation risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: cross-region latency increases during failover. Mitigation: implement warmup ramp and seeded KV cache priming where possible.
- Risk: incompatible quantized variant silently changes tokenization. Mitigation: tokenizer checksum and unit tests that compare tokenization of canonical prompt set.
- Risk: rollback oscillation. Mitigation: cooldown window and exponential backoff on auto-rollbacks.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal): merge feature flags behind 'progressive-routing' and 'deploy-compat-check'. Run internal canaries for dev-only models and verify KVs.
Phase 2 (beta customers): enable for 2 customers (non-critical) with traffic caps and manual rollback only. Collect quality metrics from shadow traffic for 48h.
Phase 3 (wider): enable geo preference and tiered-fallback for 10% of traffic on a small set of stable models. Turn on auto-rollback with conservative thresholds.
Phase 4 (GA): enable by default for new deployments; provide toggle per-project to opt-out. Publish runbook and automatic email/SMS paging on P0.
Rollback policy: auto-rollback triggers run but require human acknowledge within 15 minutes for production-critical projects. After ack, rollback finalized and variant pinned to previous stable.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Metrics to emit: per-variant request_count, error_count, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_call, cost_per_token_estimate, canary_health_score, shadow_discrepancy_rate.
Alerts: 
- CanaryHealthScore < 0.7 for 3m -> page on call (severity P1).
- p95_latency increases 2x baseline for 5m -> Slack #infra-incident and create alert ticket.
- Error rate >1% for 5m -> auto-rollback and page.
- KV-compat-check failures on deploy -> create DeployFailure ticket and notify committer.
Dashboards: per-project rollout summary, geo-routing heatmap (requests by region), fallback-paths visualization, recent auto-rollback timeline.
testing:
Unit tests: compatibility verifier (positive/negative cases), routing policy parser, fallback selection logic.
Integration tests (CI): simulate region outage, assert traffic fails over to sibling region, assert tiered fallback order, assert no writes to primary when shadowing.
Load tests: ensure route-level circuit-breaker prevents cascade; validate latency regression < 10% on steady-state.
Canary evals: run small eval set through shadow outputs and compute BLEU/EMB-similarity/LL-perplexity deltas. Thresholds stored in infra-config.
Runbook tests: runbook steps validated in tabletop exercise with SRE and PMs.
QA checklist: model upload -> verifier results -> staged rollout -> shadow validation -> canary ramp -> recovery from region failover.
